nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $a_1, \dots, a_k$ and every integer $m < 0$, the representation count $d(m; a_1, \dots, a_k)$ is $0$.
nodes.title: Negative integers have no representations

nodes.summary: If $a_1, \dots, a_k$ are positive natural numbers, then for every integer $m$ the representation count $d(m; a_1, \dots, a_k)$ is finite.
nodes.title: Finitely many representations for positive generators

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $a_1, \dots, a_k$ and an integer $m$, the representation count $d(m; a_1, \dots, a_k)$ is the number of tuples $(x_1, \dots, x_k)$ of natural numbers with $x_1 a_1 + \dots + x_k a_k = m$, counted as an extended natural number, so that it is $\infty$ when there are infinitely many such tuples.
nodes.title: Number of representations by a vector of generators

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $a_1, \dots, a_k$ and $s$, write $d(m; a)$ for the number of representations of an integer $m$ by $a = (a_1, \dots, a_k)$. An integer $g$ is the generalized Frobenius number $g(a; s) = \max \{m \in \mathbb{Z} \mid d(m; a) \le s\}$ when $d(g; a) \le s$ and $d(m; a) > s$ for every integer $m > g$.
nodes.title: Generalized Frobenius number

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $a_1, \dots, a_k$ and $s$, if the integers $g$ and $g'$ are both the generalized Frobenius number $g(a_1, \dots, a_k; s)$, then $g = g'$.
nodes.title: Uniqueness of the generalized Frobenius number
